nodes.label: Decision 13: pytest three-layer testing strategy
nodes.rationale: Unit/contract/integration layers so every failure edge case in the spec maps to at least one test; the user explicitly requested test cases and error handling. unittest rejected (pytest ecosystem richer for async); e2e-only rejected (too slow to iterate).

nodes.label: AgenticRAG MCP sidecar (Dify compose service)
nodes.rationale: Dify's SSRF proxy denies private targets by default; SSRF_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DOMAINS=agentic-rag is required in dify/docker/.env or the Dify UI save fails with "Cannot connect to MCP server" (proxy log shows TCP_DENIED/403). Dify reaches the sidecar via Docker DNS name http://agentic-rag:8080/mcp only, never localhost/127.0.0.1/host.docker.internal.

nodes.label: Decision 12: Content-hash deduplication
nodes.rationale: FR-006. SHA-256 of normalized extracted text is cheap; cross-source identity is exact-content-based (not filename-based) so it survives renames/moves; store the origin[] list on the canonical document. Near-dedup (MinHash/embedding similarity) deferred.

nodes.label: Decision 3: LanceDB + CocoIndex incremental pipeline
nodes.rationale: Explicit user requirement. CocoIndex's fingerprint-based change detection maps directly to FR-004 (add/change/delete without full rebuild); LanceDB is embedded (no server process) which fits the single-user stdio deployment. ChromaDB/Qdrant/Milvus/sqlite-vec rejected.

nodes.label: Decision 5: System 1/System 2 routing via Laya with heuristic fallback
nodes.norm_label: decision 5: system 1/system 2 routing via laya with heuristic fallback
nodes.rationale: User clarified Q1=A: run the actual Laya app locally as the decision layer. A fallback is mandatory to keep the server usable without Laya (acceptance: degradation is reported, answers still produced). Embedded-only classifier rejected by user; always-fail without Laya is unusable.

nodes.label: Decision 11: Read-only SQLite source connector
nodes.rationale: FR-002. Read-only avoids accidental mutation of user databases; hash-based change detection of rendered rows plugs into the same incremental pipeline. Direct live SQL answering deferred to v1.1.

nodes.label: FastMCP stdio server (official MCP Python SDK)
nodes.norm_label: fastmcp stdio server (official mcp python sdk)

nodes.label: Decision 2: FastMCP stdio server framework
nodes.rationale: Clarified Q5: stdio, host-spawned child process. FastMCP gives tool/resource decorators and lifecycle handling out of the box. Streamable HTTP/SSE rejected for v1 per clarification, may be added later.

nodes.label: Decision 4: Graphify kept as optional layer
nodes.norm_label: decision 4: graphify kept as optional layer
nodes.rationale: Graphify answers relationship queries ("how is X connected to Y") that pure vector similarity handles poorly, but is a superset cost (graph build time, cypher-style querying). Vector search covers core document RAG; Graphify ships as a separate MCP tool, off the fast path. Dropping it rejected because the user explicitly listed it.

nodes.label: LangGraph ReAct System 2 deliberative loop
nodes.rationale: System 2 complex research path: autonomous planning, tool routing (vector / SQL / web via Tavily-Exa-SearXNG), sufficiency checks, and a bounded iteration budget orchestrated as a LangGraph reflection loop.

nodes.label: Decision 6: LangGraph deliberative loop engine
nodes.rationale: Explicit user requirement; LangGraph provides durable graph state machines with checkpointing, well-suited to bounded-iteration loops with a configurable budget (FR-014/FR-017). Hand-rolled loop and LangChain Agents without graph rejected as fragile/less controlled.

nodes.label: Decision 10: Pluggable web search providers (Tavily/Exa/SearXNG)
nodes.rationale: FR-011 requires at least one pluggable provider; the adapter pattern keeps FR-004-style degradation behavior (SC-005) simple. A single hardwired provider rejected because the user listed three.

nodes.label: D1: HTTP client — reuse httpx
nodes.rationale: httpx is already a project dependency (used by fetch_url and the provider chain) with identical capability to requests; Constitution III (reuse installed dependencies); one HTTP stack keeps timeouts/redirects/User-Agent behavior uniform. Rejected alternative: requests — duplicates an installed capability; the reference stack's libraries are not the requirement, the extraction rules are.

nodes.label: D2: HTML parsing — beautifulsoup4 + lxml (the only new dependencies)
nodes.norm_label: d2: html parsing — beautifulsoup4 + lxml (the only new dependencies)
nodes.rationale: The user's reference implementation names this pair; grouping requires robust figure/img/data-src handling and document-order traversal that stdlib html.parser handles poorly; lxml is the fast, tolerant parser bs4 recommends (~5 MB wheel, acceptable for the container image). Rejected alternatives: stdlib html.parser (fragile for real-world HTML); lxml-only XPath (more code for the same grouping, harder to test).

nodes.label: D3: Parallel page fetching — bounded thread pool
nodes.norm_label: d3: parallel page fetching — bounded thread pool
nodes.rationale: The MCP tool layer is synchronous, so threads are the minimal concurrency change; bounded workers (max_concurrent=4) prevent engine hammering; the overall bound (FR-014, 30 s default) guarantees SC-007 — in-flight work is cut off with per-hit fallbacks. Rejected alternatives: sequential fetching (3x15 s worst case = 45 s violates FR-014); asyncio (sync tool layer would need a rewrite; no benefit at this scale).

nodes.label: D4: SSRF guard — per-hop address resolution + ipaddress check
nodes.norm_label: d4: ssrf guard — per-hop address resolution + ipaddress check
nodes.rationale: The sidecar runs on the Dify networks (postgres, redis, ssrf_proxy reachable) and search results are partially attacker-influenced, so the guard closes a real request-forgery surface; stdlib ipaddress only, no new deps; redirects are followed hop-by-hop (max 3 hops) because the classic bypass is a public URL redirecting to an internal address. Rejected alternatives: guard at DNS-resolution time only (redirect bypass); routing fetches through Dify's ssrf_proxy (couples the server to Dify deployments).

nodes.label: D5: Grouping rules — reference algorithm + spec bounds
nodes.norm_label: d5: grouping rules — reference algorithm + spec bounds
nodes.rationale: Pins the user's reference algorithm by tests: h2/h3 sections, blocks in document order, paragraphs >30 chars, real img/figure src/data-src (data: URIs skipped), urljoin absolutization, main content = article/main/body; spec adds a per-page content bound (6,000 chars default, truncation flagged), a document-order guarantee (SC-003 >=90%), and empty-section tolerance (JS-only pages fall back, never crash). Rejected alternatives: readability-style full-text extraction (loses the text-image grouping that is the feature's core); tables/code-block capture (deferred, out of scope).

nodes.label: D8: Configuration surface — [web.research] block in config.toml
nodes.norm_label: d8: configuration surface — [web.research] block in config.toml
nodes.rationale: All bounds in one place with sensible defaults (max_pages=3 cap 5, per_page_chars=6000, fetch_timeout_s=15.0, overall_timeout_s=30.0, max_concurrent=4) so no new user decisions are required at runtime; engine provenance and dedup are behavior, not config.

nodes.label: FR-005: Document-order grouped section extraction
nodes.rationale: The user's core objective: preserve the original page outline — each section is a heading plus its paragraphs and belonging images interleaved in document order (h2 → p → img → p), never 'all text, then all images'; grouped sections, not raw page dumps, are what pass to the LLM.

nodes.label: FR-008: Honest snippet fallback — never silently missing, never fabricated
nodes.norm_label: fr-008: honest snippet fallback — never silently missing, never fabricated
nodes.rationale: Constitution IV (honest): an unfetchable, unparseable, JS-only, paywalled, timed-out, or SSRF-blocked page carries its search snippet explicitly marked as fallback — content is never silently omitted and never invented.

nodes.label: FR-013: SSRF guard — refuse private/loopback/link-local fetch targets
nodes.norm_label: fr-013: ssrf guard — refuse private/loopback/link-local fetch targets
nodes.rationale: The sidecar runs on the Dify networks where internal services live, so unguarded fetches of attacker-influenced search-result URLs are a real request-forgery surface; a blocked page falls back to its snippet marked with the block reason (FR-008). The pre-existing fetch_url tool's identical exposure is a separate follow-up, out of this feature's scope.

nodes.label: US2: Outline-Preserving Grouped Page Content for the LLM (P1)
nodes.norm_label: us2: outline-preserving grouped page content for the llm (p1)
nodes.rationale: This is the user's core objective — 'a nice and useful output to pass to the LLM'; the grouped structure is what makes scraped pages usable as agent evidence instead of noise, and Constitution IV demands content is never silently missing and never invented.

nodes.label: Chatflow Basic (AgenticRAG Agent)
nodes.rationale: Dify advanced-chat DSL whose Agent (Agentic Strategy) node is wired to the 'Agentic RAG' MCP provider (agentic-rag). AMBIGUOUS flag: the app and node descriptions say 'all 8 tools' but the tools list actually wires 11 tools (ask, search, sources_add, sources_list, sources_remove, sources_sync, graph_query, status, web_search, fetch_url, web_research).

nodes.label: MCP Sidecar Docker Compose (standalone)
nodes.rationale: Standalone local run of the sidecar with NO Dify networks; builds from repo root (needs pyproject.toml + src/); mounts ~/.config/agentic-rag-mcp (config + LanceDB state) and the Hugging Face cache (decision-model + embedder checkpoints); 28080:8080 publish avoids the crowded 8080.

nodes.label: agenticrag-deploy Skill
nodes.rationale: The same runbook content ships as the agenticrag-deploy skill at ~/.config/kilo/skills/agenticrag-deploy/SKILL.md.

nodes.label: Deploy Steps 0-7
nodes.rationale: Step 0 prerequisites (Python 3.12+, ~4 GB disk, ~2.5 GB free RAM) -> 1 pipx install + agentic-rag-mcp --init -> 2 tune [decider] timeout above measured warm latency -> 3 build and run sidecar (28080:8080) -> 4 Dify wiring -> 5 SearXNG -> 6 ingest sources -> 7 verify.

nodes.label: Port Convention (host 28080 sidecar, 28888 SearXNG, container 8080)
nodes.rationale: Avoid the crowded common ports on the HOST: use 28080 for the AgenticRAG sidecar and 28888 for SearXNG; container-internal ports stay 8080 in both cases. agentic-rag:28080 does not exist - container-to-container is always :8080.

nodes.label: SearXNG Service
nodes.rationale: The stock image ships WITHOUT the JSON API enabled but the AgenticRAG provider uses format=json, so settings.yml must enable json formats; host publish 28888->8080; first query after container recreation is slow while engines warm up.

nodes.label: SSRF Allowlist Step (SSRF_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DOMAINS=agentic-rag)
nodes.rationale: Without SSRF_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DOMAINS=agentic-rag in the Dify compose .env (then docker compose up -d ssrf_proxy), Dify shows 'Cannot connect to MCP server' because the ssrf proxy blocks private targets.

nodes.label: 5-Minute Verification Battery
nodes.rationale: healthz must return status ok and tools/list must return 10 tools, then exercise status, search, ask, sources_list/add/sync/remove, web_search (live), fetch_url (live), graph_query (honest FeatureDisabled error).

nodes.label: Agentic Strategy Node (FunctionCalling)
nodes.rationale: FunctionCalling agent strategy, model deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash via langgenius/openrouter/openrouter, maximum_iterations 10, minimum Dify version 1.7.0; instructions: use fetch_url date_utc for current time, prefer web_research over web_search for real page content, report graph_query FeatureDisabled honestly, confirm before destructive sources_remove. DEPLOY.md separately cites a 'Dify 1.17' identifier-vs-UUID edit bug (version ambiguity unresolved).

nodes.label: agentic-rag MCP Sidecar Container
nodes.rationale: The agentic-rag container runs the MCP server statelessly for Dify, listening 0.0.0.0:8080 internally (published to host 28080); Dify reaches it only via container DNS at agentic-rag:8080, never via host ports.

nodes.label: Dify Stack (nginx, api, postgres, ssrf_proxy)
nodes.rationale: Docker compose stack (nginx, docker-api-1, ssrf_proxy, postgres) on networks docker_default + docker_ssrf_proxy_network; the browser reaches nginx on 10.0.1.75:80 / kilo.clinic.com.hk.

nodes.label: Port Convention (NETWORK.md)
nodes.rationale: Dify UI to sidecar: http://agentic-rag:8080/mcp (never 28080, never localhost); host to sidecar: localhost:28080/healthz; sidecar to SearXNG: http://searxng:8080 (config [web.searxng] url); host to SearXNG: localhost:28888 with JSON API test /search?q=t&format=json returning 200.

nodes.label: Dify ssrf_proxy
nodes.rationale: Dify api sends MCP JSON-RPC via ssrf_proxy:3128, which forwards to http://agentic-rag:8080/mcp - the MCP path; a missing SSRF allowlist entry causes 'Cannot connect to MCP server'.

nodes.label: Agentic RAG MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Agentic RAG as an MCP server: 97 tests, contract-preserved responses, provenance on every decision; spec 002 (laya-reflexion-nodes) supersedes spec 001's routing/loop design; stdio host config uses command agentic-rag-mcp.

nodes.label: ask Tool
nodes.rationale: Agentic Q&A with citations; every response carries decision (route, complexity, sufficiency, provenance, latency_ms) and reflections (per-trial evaluator scores/verdicts/critiques); the response field set is the non-negotiable backward-compatible client contract.

nodes.label: Dual-System Workflow
nodes.rationale: System 1 (embedded decision node) routes every request in one cheap pass; only deliberative_reasoning and live_web routes escalate to the System 2 LangGraph reflexion graph with self-correcting, memory-conditioned retries.

nodes.label: Fallback Provenance (decision_node | fallback)
nodes.rationale: If the decision node is unavailable/invalid/timed-out (or [decider] enabled=false), a keyword heuristic routes and responses are marked provenance 'fallback' (FR-003 of spec 002); provenance is binary - decision_node or fallback - with no third value.

nodes.label: Known Pin: faster-whisper==1.2.1 vs PyAV 19
nodes.rationale: faster-whisper==1.2.1 calls av.open(..., metadata_errors='ignore') which was removed in PyAV 19; the vendored copy is patched so unreadable audio files are skipped with a reason instead of crashing the batch; upstream fix: pin PyAV<19 or upgrade faster-whisper when fixed.

nodes.label: fetch_url Tool
nodes.rationale: Fetches a live page; returns date_utc from the HTTP Date header as an accurate live UTC clock for current time/date questions (cached search snippets are not accurate).

nodes.label: graph_query Tool
nodes.rationale: Optional Graphify layer over graphify-out/graph.json; disabled by default ([features] graphify = false) and returns an honest FeatureDisabled error when off; enable and build with the graphify skill.

nodes.label: LanceDB
nodes.rationale: Vector store for retrieval; starts empty on a fresh host (state lives in ~/.config/agentic-rag-mcp/), filled by source ingestion; the watcher re-syncs every 5 minutes.

nodes.label: search Tool
nodes.rationale: Direct vector search over LanceDB without synthesis; args query and limit.

nodes.label: sources_add Tool
nodes.rationale: Registers a knowledge-base source; type local_folder needs config.path, type sqlite needs config.db_path/table/template.

nodes.label: sources_list Tool
nodes.rationale: Lists registered sources with health and sync metadata; deploy verification expects sources to report healthy.

nodes.label: sources_remove Tool
nodes.rationale: Removes a source by id - destructive; drops documents whose last origin was this source.

nodes.label: sources_sync Tool
nodes.rationale: Manual incremental sync (optional source_id) - the instant alternative to the 5-minute watcher auto-update cycle.

nodes.label: status Tool
nodes.rationale: Server health: decision-node provenance, per-source health, index counters.

nodes.label: System 1 Decision Node (embedded Laya model)
nodes.rationale: Embedded Laya decision model (convaiinnovations/laya, ~1.7 GB download, ~2 GB RAM loaded) routes every ask in one pass with no text generation: route choice (direct_retrieval | deliberative_reasoning | live_web | source_management), complexity 1-10, sufficiency boolean; warm latency is hardware-dependent (~140 ms Apple Silicon, ~7.4 s small ARM cloud CPU) so [decider] timeout must exceed measured latency; pre-loads in the background at startup.

nodes.label: System 2 Reflexion Graph (Actor - Evaluator - Self-Reflector - Episodic Memory)
nodes.norm_label: system 2 reflexion graph (actor - evaluator - self-reflector - episodic memory)
nodes.rationale: LangGraph reflexion graph for deliberative routes: Actor, then Evaluator (score+verdict), then Self-Reflector, then Episodic Memory; the loop is gated ONLY by the evaluator, the union of all reflections conditions every retry, and it is bounded by max_iterations.

nodes.label: web_research Tool
nodes.rationale: Grouped deep web research (spec 003): multi-engine search via the provider chain, per-page outline-preserving scrape (text + belonging images in document order), bounded for the LLM by [web.research] (max_pages 3 cap 5, per_page_chars 6000, fetch_timeout_s 15, overall_timeout_s 30, max_concurrent 4), honest snippet fallbacks, rendered HTML artifact per page.

nodes.label: web_search Tool
nodes.rationale: Live web search via SearXNG with fallback chain searxng, then tavily, then exa; snippets are cached, so never trusted for exact time/date.

nodes.label: Contract Preservation (Principle I)
nodes.rationale: Client-facing tool contracts (the ask response field set and MCP tool schemas) must stay backward-compatible because consumers (Dify chatflows, MCP hosts) must never break on a server upgrade; new fields are additive only; breaking changes require a spec amendment documenting the migration.

nodes.label: Honest Answers (Principle IV)
nodes.rationale: The system never fabricates: no evidence yields 'no relevant information was found'; budget exhaustion yields a low-confidence flag; disabled features yield explicit FeatureDisabled errors; every routing decision carries provenance (decision_node | fallback) - there is no third value.

nodes.label: Minimal Dependencies (Principle III)
nodes.rationale: Reuse ladder before adding anything: stdlib, then platform, then already-installed dependency, then new dependency; vendored third-party code carries its license header and a re-vendor upgrade path; new runtime services are a last resort and must degrade gracefully when absent.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Replacement (Principle V)
nodes.rationale: Superseding work retires the old design, it does not deprecate it: old code paths are deleted (no dead code), the spec carries a Supersedes record, the client contract is preserved field-for-field, and configuration for retired components is removed with them.

nodes.label: Tests-First (Principle II)
nodes.rationale: Every non-trivial behavior lands with its runnable check written before implementation (unit/integration/contract per tests/ layout); the full suite (97 tests) must be green before commit; tests are never weakened to pass - fix the code or a genuinely dishonest fixture.

nodes.label: Fresh-Host Deployment Runbook
nodes.rationale: Runtime state lives OUTSIDE the repo in ~/.config/agentic-rag-mcp/ (config, LanceDB data, model checkpoints) so a fresh clone starts empty; the runbook recreates everything from git clone to a verified MCP sidecar, optionally wired into Dify.

nodes.label: Network Topology (Dify - AgenticRAG - Host)
nodes.rationale: Who talks to whom, on which port, and why. Two rules: Dify never touches host ports (its path runs entirely inside the Docker networks on internal port 8080, so changing the host port to 28080 required zero Dify changes) and 28080/28888 are host-only windows whose removal would not affect Dify.

nodes.label: AgenticRAG Constitution
nodes.rationale: House governance for all /speckit.* commands: amendments require documented rationale in the amending spec's Clarifications section; violations surface as CRITICAL convergence findings; lazy engineering (shortest working diff, deletion over addition, YAGNI) never overrides Principles I and IV.

nodes.label: D6: Test strategy + error-handling matrix
nodes.rationale: The user's binding note ('create test cases and add error handling') + Constitution II: each matrix row must have a runnable test before its implementation is marked done; the matrix doubles as the implementation task list's acceptance spine; no live web in CI — search is mocked at the provider interface and pages come from local HTTP fixture servers and file fixtures.

nodes.label: US1: Multi-Engine Live Search (P1)
nodes.rationale: Every downstream capability (scraping, grouping, rendering) depends on a dependable, broad search layer, and the existing web tool is already in production use by the chatflow, so its contract must hold. litellm NOT adopted (user decision, 2026-10-09): it adds 23 transitive packages (incl. the AWS SDK) for three stable ~30-line REST calls the provider chain already performs; its search API is single-provider-per-call so the fallback chain remains our code either way; env-var-only config conflicts with config.toml; Constitution III (minimal dependencies) and V favor retention — new engines (e.g. perplexity) join as small adapters on the existing pattern.

nodes.label: D7: Rendering — stdlib string templates, no engine
nodes.norm_label: d7: rendering — stdlib string templates, no engine
nodes.rationale: Constitution III (no new dependency); the rendered artifact is review-only — the LLM consumes the structured sections. Rejected alternatives: Jinja2 (a dependency for ~20 lines of markup); reusing bs4 to emit parsed trees (grouping already produces clean structures; direct templating is simpler and testable).

nodes.label: US3: Human-Readable Rendering of Grouped Results (P3)
nodes.norm_label: us3: human-readable rendering of grouped results (p3)
nodes.rationale: The LLM consumes the structured sections; rendering is review/diagnostic value — useful but not load-bearing for answer quality.

nodes.label: FR-011: New web_research MCP Tool
nodes.rationale: Decided in validation pass 3: the MCP surface is a new additive web_research tool composing the existing provider chain, rather than modifying web_search — replacement-vs-additive framing per Constitution I / FR-002.

nodes.label: FR-002: web_search Contract Freeze
nodes.rationale: Constitution I Contract Preservation: the existing web_search response shape is pinned by the existing test_web_providers.py regression suite; the new capability is additive (a new web_research tool) rather than a replacement, so the frozen contract stays byte-identical.

nodes.label: FR-008: Honest Snippet Fallback (Every Hit Yields Content)
nodes.norm_label: fr-008: honest snippet fallback (every hit yields content)
nodes.rationale: Constitution IV Honest Answers: snippet fallbacks are explicit and marked with status_reason, empty results are honest (all engines down yields hits: [] with a non-null error), and nothing is fabricated — content is never empty.

nodes.label: FR-010: Standalone render_html Returned Inline
nodes.rationale: Decided in validation pass 3: rendered HTML is returned inline in the response within the per-page bound rather than stored or served separately — research results are per-request and ephemeral (no storage changes), and the artifact is standalone HTML openable without a server, with section order mirroring sections.

nodes.label: FR-012: ask Live-Web Evidence Upgrade
nodes.rationale: Resolved in the double-clarify pass: the ask pipeline's live-web evidence upgrades to grouped scraping for both consumers; the internal evidence shape (content per evidence item, no render) is not a client contract and may evolve.

nodes.label: FR-013: SSRF Guard on Scraped Fetches
nodes.norm_label: fr-013: ssrf guard on scraped fetches
nodes.rationale: The server runs as a Docker sidecar on Dify networks, so scraped fetches must refuse private/loopback/link-local destinations (including via redirects) with a snippet fallback — never fetched. Honors the constitution preamble that security measures are never simplified away; the equivalent fetch_url guard is a separate follow-up, out of scope for this feature.

nodes.label: ScrapeResult (states: ok | fallback | blocked | failed)
nodes.rationale: State transitions per hit: fetch -> guard-check -> blocked, or parse -> failed/empty -> fallback, or extract -> truncated -> ok. Any non-ok terminal state yields the search snippet as the hit's content, marked with status_reason — honest fallback so content is never empty.

nodes.label: Error-Handling Test Matrix (research D6)
nodes.rationale: Binding user note: the plan must create test cases and add error handling as first-class deliverables — every fallback/error path gets a runnable test (Constitution II). One test per fallback path: timeout, JS-only page, HTTP error, private-address block, oversized page, engine-down, all-engines-down; CI runs against local fixture pages with the engine chain mocked (no live web).

nodes.label: MCP Tool Contracts: Agentic RAG MCP Server
nodes.norm_label: mcp tool contracts: agentic rag mcp server
nodes.rationale: Degradation over failure: auth failures mark a source degraded (health: degraded, health_reason: auth_expired) instead of throwing; SufficiencyExhausted is returned as confidence: low, not an RPC error; DecisionLayerUnavailable downgrades to the fallback path and is noted in trace; stack traces never cross the wire. Partially superseded 2026-10-08: ask additionally carries decision and reflections, and web_search/fetch_url tools were added (additive; all contracts below remain in force).

nodes.label: Agentic RAG MCP Server Feature Specification
nodes.norm_label: agentic rag mcp server feature specification
nodes.rationale: Priority rationale: sourced Q&A is the core value (without it every other capability is dead weight); stale answers destroy trust, so incremental near-real-time indexing is a stated differentiator; agentic deep research depends on the retrieval substrate; live web adds recency but the system is useful without it. Supersession: the single-label classifier, keyword-heuristic primary routing, and monolithic deliberation loop were replaced by spec 002's embedded System 1 decision node and LangGraph reflexion graph; ingestion, storage, sources, contracts, and all other FRs remain in force.

nodes.label: Data Model: Grouped Web Research
nodes.rationale: Design decision: all entities are per-request and ephemeral — nothing persists beyond the web_research response or the ask evidence pass (no storage or LanceDB/state changes); the rendered artifact travels inline in the response.

nodes.label: Implementation Plan: Grouped Web Research
nodes.rationale: Plan decisions: httpx reused for page fetching (over requests); renderer is stdlib string templates (no template engine); research code lives beside the providers in search/web/research.py (one new module, no new package); the SSRF guard is a function inside research.py with a ponytail note for later extraction if fetch_url adopts it; tests are layered unit/integration/contract with the web_search shape frozen and the web_research schema pinned; target platform is a Linux venv plus the deployed Docker sidecar on Dify networks.

nodes.label: Decision: Add beautifulsoup4 + lxml for Outline Extraction
nodes.norm_label: decision: add beautifulsoup4 + lxml for outline extraction
nodes.rationale: beautifulsoup4 + lxml are the only new dependencies: outline extraction is a new capability and stdlib html.parser is too fragile for figure/img/data-src handling. Accepted trade-off: the lxml binary wheel adds ~5 MB to the Docker image. The renderer deliberately uses stdlib string templates (no template engine) and httpx is reused over requests for page fetching.

nodes.label: Decision: Reject litellm, Retain Existing Provider Chain
nodes.norm_label: decision: reject litellm, retain existing provider chain
nodes.rationale: litellm was rejected on recorded evidence (spec Clarifications, validation pass 2) and the existing searxng/tavily/exa provider chain retained — Constitution III Minimal Dependencies forbids new search dependencies; no litellm appears in the plan's dependency list.
